newsitem.title: UK: Royal Sun eases as profits fail to impress.
newsitem.headline: Royal Sun eases as profits fail to impress.

text.p: Shares in Royal Sun Alliance Plc erased initial gains and turned lower in late morning trading on Thursday after investors took a closer look at the insurer's annual results, analysts and dealers said.
By 1144 GMT, the shares were off 8-1/2p 495, having climbed as high as 515 initially after the group said it intended to seek approval for a share buyback.
Analysts and dealers said that confusion over when and if a share buyback would be implemented contributed to the decline in the share price.
They said the results were generally in line, but that Royal Sun's net asset value hadn't improved much, also weighing on the share price.
"The figures weren't terrible, they were just boring and unimpressive," said one analyst. "The NAV (net asset value) was disappointing, their intentions for a share buyback weren't clear."
"I think this is just an unwinding of unrealistic premiums in the share price," the analyst added.

Meanwhile, brokerage SocGen trimmed its 1997 profit forecast for the group to 178 million stg from 190 million stg. It also cut its 1998 profit estimate to 195 million stg from 210 stg, and maintained its "hold" rating.
Earlier, Royal Sun posted annual pre-exceptional operating profits of 706 million stg.
Elsewhere in the sector, shares in General Accident Plc remained firmer, gaining 6p to 860, while shares in Commercial Union Plc advanced 10-1/2p to 741-1/2. --London newsroom +44 171 542 5106
